findings.finding: Round 3 refuses a role executable whose content equals another role's executable or an enrolled interpreter (R52, R53, and a verity-only collision probe), but a role closure may still list another role's executable or the interpreter by path: path and content sharing stays allowed inside the single resident-role owner class (needed for the shared SERVER/WORKER interpreter), and no capture field identifies the process image (/proc/<pid>/exe); files and executableMaps are compared only as sets. Probes, full bundles rebound, positives 0 and 1: EFFECT_GATE filePaths plus the gate capture's files and executableMaps extended with /opt/planeon/bin/harness-capacity-broker, with /opt/planeon/python/3.12.14/bin/python3.12, or with python3.12 and the worker script harness-live-probe-exec are all ACCEPTED by check_qualification; so are OBSERVER (interpreterPath null) loading python3.12, SERVER loading the gate artifact, and a gate executable byte-identical to a library listed in the broker closure. Those observations are indistinguishable from the broker binary or Python running in the gate's cgroup and domain. Decision 5 ('the gate is native only') and the Gate identity row ('a copied broker or Python binary cannot pass as the gate') therefore hold for copies at the gate path but not for the enrolled originals, and the intent of spec 4.4 ('puts the gate under the BROKER key or path') is reachable through the closure. v1 has the same closure model; the native-only rule and the gate are v2 additions.

questionAnswers.Q2: Yes. check_capture's WORKER branch requires capPermitted, capEffective, capAmbient and capInheritable to equal [], capBounding to be duplicate-free and a subset of the BROKER's enrolled set (schema const CAP_BPF, CAP_NET_ADMIN, CAP_SETGID, CAP_SETUID), noNewPrivs equal to the record's const 1, uid and gid equal to the record's WORKER values (schema minimum 10000, so non-root) and threadsUniform true; every other role keeps permitted = effective = bounding = enrolled with ambient and inheritable empty. C06 and C07 refuse, A04 accepts an empty bounding set, the positives carry the inherited broker set, and probes refuse a {CAP_SETPCAP} bounding set, no_new_privs 0 and non-empty inheritable, ambient or effective sets while accepting {CAP_SETUID}. It is no weaker than claimed: per capabilities(7) the bounding set enters P'(permitted) only through file permitted capabilities, and dropping an entry needs CAP_SETPCAP while the set is inherited at fork and preserved across execve (so the premise holds); per PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS, file capabilities and set-user-ID bits are non-functional under no_new_privs; with empty permitted, inheritable and ambient sets and a non-root uid, capset cannot add to the inheritable set and an ambient raise needs both. D5 is a deliberate, disclosed relaxation of the reviewed spec's 5.3 WORKER row (bounding equal to the empty set) taken as the owner's decision; its stated carry to W01's record and T04 is not evidenced in the reviewed bytes (P2).
questionAnswers.Q3: Mostly faithful, with disclosed deferrals and one partly enforced decision. Encoded: 4.1 (record and profile versions, the closed five roles all required, the gate present without a listener in zero-resource mode, closed lifecycle subjects with digest, domain and entry rule, closed backend keys bound to the implementation profile); 4.2 (exact slice, service and leaf paths, the delegated service with exactly broker and probe-worker and no direct members, leaves without children, gate, writer and containment artifact paths, a 0555 root-owned gate artifact through the actual-executable rule and root-owned file observations, the gate listener as the signed KUBERNETES_API_PROXY endpoint); 4.4 (every rejection vector: X01-X13, R01-R07, R43, R50, R55, R75, C14-C25, L11, L12, M02-M10); 5.1 (commands {7,15,16}, pin layout and label, BPF_F_ALLOW_MULTI, helper-free, map-free and unique programs, jit_harden 0 or 1, effective = local = the enrolled program); 5.2 (lockdown integrity, enforcing with a pinned policy digest, the three booleans, modules_disabled, kexec_load_disabled, ptrace_scope 3, unprivileged_bpf_disabled 1, module-set digest, a boot-bound seal marker on tmpfs, containment absent); 5.3 (uids, capability sets with D5, seccomp mode 2 with KILL_PROCESS and a filter digest, no_new_privs 1, RLIMIT_CORE 0, the CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE coupling, fixed per-role domains). Not encoded and deferred: exact filters (W02d), label values and the permission matrix, program-object ownership and pin permissions, confinement of the qualk8s types, root-login confinement and 'no unconfined or permissive domain anywhere on the host' (these rest on the pinned policy digest and W02e; data constrains only planeon and backend domains), POLICY_WRITER's steady-state row (decision 8), the identity closure (W02g) and unit-file properties (RefuseManualStart, Delegate). No spec rule is weakened apart from the owner-decided D5 relaxation; the additions (decisions 9, 10, 11 and the native-only gate) are stricter. Decisions 1-11 are listed with rationale; decision 5's native-only property is enforced only against copies (P1), decision 8's enforcement for the slice root rests on an unstated kernel rule (P5), decision 4's separate-process rule is enforced (probe), and decision 6's consequence is disclosed.
questionAnswers.Q4: Yes, some violating inputs still pass; none reaches MAJOR in this review. Accepted (full bundles rebound where the record changes): a gate, observer or server closure listing another role's executable or python3.12, including a gate that loads the broker binary, or python3.12 plus the worker script (P1); a census listing unpopulated descendants of role cgroups or a third broker leaf, or reporting live role cgroups or planeon.slice as unpopulated, beside role captures that report none (P3); a WORKER co-member that is also the KUBELET process (P4); processes directly in planeon.slice, which no field can report (P5); SERVER pids.max 1 with four threads (P6); nested backend cgroups, system:masters among SCHEDULER or APISERVER identities (W02g scope) and arbitrary but consistent label values (W02e scope); and, by stated caller obligation, proxy-invalid profiles, incomplete v1 histories, a false empty-history attestation and v1 records from another machine. Sound where tested: the census refuses populated unenrolled cgroups, including role-cgroup descendants, children of the containment cgroup and non-canonical aliases of enrolled paths (L11, L12, probes); host-wide role-domain counts refuse role-domain processes outside role cgroups (Q07, server and worker probes); role subtrees for all five roles and the broker service (C19-C25, OBSERVER probe); worker membership by label, uid, no_new_privs, seccomp and descent, with grandchildren accepted and cycles and sibling workers refused; the allow-list and implementation profile (R57-R66); content-distinct executables including verity-only collisions (R52, R53); the seal marker's binding of the boot and every (role, hook, program, digest) (R54 and a boot probe; a consistent recomputation is accepted, as disclosed); migration with an attested empty history (M08-M10) and the full-string v1 nonce scan; decision 4's separate processes. A diff against the round-2 model found no dropped check: the denylist became a stricter schema allow-list, by_content split into by_sha256 and by_verity, and WORKER members are now unique by pid.

All 38 schema-level negatives are single top-level errors. Each negative's intent matches the rule that fires (R61 and R66 now fire as schema consts, which makes the model's planeon-domain and shared-domain backend checks unreachable; R73 fires as custody). questionAnswers.Q6: Yes.
